items.title: At least 47 dead in Colombia after powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake
items.description: At least six airports have suspended operations as Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella says he has "directly assumed leadership of the emergency response".

items.title: 'Loyalty doesn't pay': Car insurers asked to explain soaring premiums
items.description: The corporate regulator ASIC has taken aim at major car insurers, finding that the companies are not explaining why customers' premiums are rising faster than inflation.

items.title: Coalition calls on Albanese to apologise to Japan's PM over melon gesture
items.description: The Australian prime minister has landed in hot water over a gesture involving two melons, which his office insists was not referring to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's body.

items.title: Former ambassador warns Australia's ties with China could spiral again
items.description: Australia's former ambassador to China says the relationship between the two countries remains fragile and vulnerable to shocks, saying stability will "remain a goal, not a given" for Canberra.

items.title: Senator blasts 'floating sweatshop' cruise ships
items.description: The Anti-Slavery Commissioner is calling for change after Carnival cruise staff alleged conditions one senator called a "floating sweatshop".

items.title: How a simple request for AI to book a gym class exposed a major threat
items.description: When Andrew asked his AI personal assistant to book him a spot in a gym class, he had no idea he would accidentally initiate an autonomous cyber attack.

items.title: What have we learnt from Origin Energy's data breach?
items.description: Three weeks ago, Origin Energy announced that 900,000 current and former customers had their personal data accessed. What have we learnt about our data safety online since?

items.title: Thailand rocked by second shooting tragedy in three days
items.description: A gunman is arrested after firing shots at a local government office on the outskirts of Bangkok with a former member of parliament accused of killing a former colonel whom he had known for years, and wounding his driver.

items.title: How far does the JobSeeker allowance actually go?
items.description: JobSeeker exists to support Australian's when they can't find work, but how far does that money actually go? The number of long-term JobSeeker recipients has almost tripled since 2012, despite hundreds of millions of dollars being paid to private equity-controlled firms to find people jobs. So, how are the 900,000 people on JobSeeker making ends meet?

items.title: Ukraine kills 13 in drone attack on Russian city of Nizhnekamsk
items.description: Russian investigators say they have opened a criminal case into what they qualified as a terrorist attack 800km east of Moscow, saying that Ukraine had struck residential areas and that a child was among those civilians killed.

items.title: 'Generational change': Melissa Donnelly named as new ACTU boss
items.description: The 44-year-old inherits the trade union movement while it is enjoying a golden era of political influence, but also faces a long-term decline in membership and a fight for the rights of workers in the AI boom.

items.title: Adelaide waterfalls roar to life as reservoirs receive decade-high deluge
items.description: In scenes reminiscent of tropical Queensland, waterfalls in the Adelaide Hills have been whipped into raging torrents as reservoirs receive 18 billion litres of water in just 24 hours.

items.title: Police believe 'body' found in suitcase by road was a sex doll
items.description: Police sources say a "body" found in a suitcase in southern NSW is believed to be a sex doll, rather than the remains of a woman as first feared.

items.title: Woman cleared of Cassius Turvey's murder avoids jail for driving with no licence
items.description: Aleesha Gilmore, found not guilty of murdering Perth school boy Cassius Turvey, has avoided an immediate prison term for breaching the terms of her suspended sentence.

items.title: My Brilliant Career cast reflects on 'defiant' Netflix adaptation
items.description: An adaptation of the Miles Franklin classic My Brilliant Career will come to Netflix this week, with members of the cast and crew saying the defiance in this production lives in the expansion of the world Franklin created.

items.title: Five accused of using dating apps for homophobic attacks in Melbourne
items.description: The arrest of the five males brings the number of people accused of similar attacks around the state to almost 50.

items.title: Trial begins in case of man accused of Bogie triple murder
items.description: The trial of a man accused of murdering three people on a Queensland cattle property in 2022 has begun.

items.title: Australia has the most expensive cigarettes in the world, and now a booming black market
items.description: After decades as a world leader in tobacco control, Australia now finds itself in troubled waters. But those trying to find solutions are far from on the same page.

items.title: Former championship winning team cut from A-Leagues
items.description: The Australian Professional Leagues have terminated Western United's A-Leagues participation agreement, meaning the club won't be returning to the top flight.

items.title: Meaty mushrooms are the star of the show in these five dishes
items.description: Mushrooms are affordable, flavoursome and can make a dish feel rich and meatier.

items.title: How Elliot won Race Around the World in 'opportunity of a lifetime'
items.description: After 100 days telling stories from the furthest corners of the globe, Race Around the World winner Elliot Constable credits one particular approach for his success.

items.title: Frydenberg says he will not be called as royal commission witness
items.description: Former treasurer Josh Frydenberg said he made a submission to the commission and indicated his willingness to appear as a witness.

items.title: The end of the low interest rate era is here and it weighs on house prices
items.description: We seem to have flipped from worrying about rising house prices to worrying about falling house prices. Well, some of us have, anyway.

items.title: ICAC explores lobbyist's role in right-wing Liberal group's alleged corruption
items.description: Lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood said a right-wing Liberal Party factional group at the centre of a corruption watchdog inquiry became so "toxic" he encouraged his friends to leave it.

items.title: Victorian teachers to vote on new pay offer before strike
items.description: The new pay offer includes a $2,000 lump-sum payment if they agree to the deal, which would head off a third statewide strike.
